# 太真玉帝四極明科經-六朝

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A five-juan Shàngqīng 上清 codebook, preserved in the *Zhèngtǒng Dàozàng* 正統道藏 (DZ 0184 / CT 184 = TC 184), 洞真部 戒律類. The title — read with *míng* 明 as a graphic substitution for *méng* 盟 (sworn) — is among many similar codebook-titles named in the original Yáng-Xǔ Shàngqīng revelations (most of those imaginary titles never realised in surviving texts). The five juan are placed under the authority of the Five Palaces of the Capital of Mystery (Xuándū 玄都) and under the jurisdiction of the Five Emperors of the Five Directions; each juan comprises twenty-four articles, dispersing the codebook's prescriptions across a hundred-and-twenty-article structure that encompasses the rules for the transmission of the sacred scriptures (chiefly Shàngqīng but with Língbǎo 靈寶 and Sāndòng 三洞 entries also: 4.2b, 3b) and the rites to be observed by those in possession of them.

**Abstract**

Isabelle Robinet, in Schipper & Verellen eds., *The Taoist Canon* (2004) 1:193–194 (§1.B.2 Shàngqīng), traces the work's complex textual history. A *Sìjí míngkē* is explicitly cited by such early Shàngqīng works as *[DZ 1331 Dòngzhēn shàngqīng shénzhōu qīzhuàn qībiàn wǔtiān jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b1466)* (29a) and *[DZ 1321 Dòngzhēn tàishàng bāsù zhēnjīng xiūxí gōngyè miàojué](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b1454)* (2b), but those quotations do not appear in the present text — meaning the present *Sìjí míngkē* is a recension later than the late-fourth-century citations. Closer correspondences appear in later sources: *[DZ 1314 Dòngzhēn tàishàng sūlíng dòngyuán dàyǒu miàojīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b1448)* gives an exact rendering of a passage; quotations in *[DZ 1332 Dòngzhēn tàishàng tàixiāo lángshū](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b1466)* 2a–13b, *[DZ 1203 Tàishàng sāntiān zhèngfǎ jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b1339)* 8b–9a, and the *Wúshàng bìyào* 無上祕要 all have equivalents in the present work. The preface incorporates excerpts from *[DZ 1344 Dòngzhēn tàishàng shuō zhìhuì xiāomó zhēnjīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b1486)* 1.5a–b and a quotation from the now-lost *Tàizhēn kē* 太真科, also found in *Sāndòng zhūnáng* (*SDZN*) 7.16b. Analysis of the contents and quotation-set indicates that the present text has undergone several revisions tracking the scriptural development of Shàngqīng; in its current state it is later than *[DZ 1314 Sūlíng dòngyuán](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b1448)* (giving a more coherent synthesis of the scriptures) and later than the Língbǎo revelation (*ca.* 400), but earlier than *[DZ 1203 Sāntiān zhèngfǎ jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR5/KR5b/KR5b1339)*, whose quotations match the present version exactly. The frontmatter accordingly brackets composition to the Six Dynasties (early-fifth to late-sixth century), with TC's specification of "Six Dynasties (220–589)" understood as the *received-recension* span.
